title: Weak Choice Atlas — starter catalogue
scope: Broad coverage from the start. This is an extensible inventory, not an exhaustive enumeration or a certified implication graph.
status: Initial public catalogue; relation review levels are shown individually.
counts_note: Records include parameterized families, equivalent anchors, ZF theorems and research candidates; 88 is not a count of pairwise inequivalent weak axioms.

notation.C(I,F): Every family (A_i) indexed by an index set of type I, with each A_i nonempty and of type F, admits a function c with c(i) in A_i.
notation.finite: Finite, with fiber nonemptiness already required.
notation.omega: Index set omega; countably infinite families. Finite families are handled in ZF.
notation.countable: At most countable, meaning injectible into omega; no enumerations are supplied as additional data.
notation.WO: Well-orderable (or given well-ordered index); existence of well-orders on individual fibers is not a simultaneous choice of well-orders.
notation.P(R): A subset of the real numbers, required nonempty when a fiber.
notation.Baire: Every countable intersection of dense open sets is dense.
notation.compact: Every open cover has a finite subcover.

editorial_rules: Candidate means awaiting editorial admission; it does not mean an open mathematical problem.
Definition evidence is not proof of any implication or nonimplication.
ZF and ZFA have separate relation views; transfer requires its own justified evidence.

principles.name: Full Tychonoff theorem
principles.definition: For every set I and every indexed family ((X_i,τ_i))_{i∈I} of compact topological spaces, the Cartesian product ∏_{i∈I}X_i with the product topology is compact. Compact means that every open cover has a finite subcover.
principles.notes: No separation axiom (Hausdorff or T₁) is assumed. No point of the product is supplied, and the conclusion does not explicitly assert nonemptiness: the empty space is compact. This compactness-only assertion is nevertheless equivalent to AC. It remains AC-equivalent if one restricts to families whose product is already known to be nonempty; see the added-point proof. Separately, asserting that arbitrary families of nonempty compact spaces have nonempty products yields AC directly by equipping arbitrary nonempty sets with indiscrete topologies. For compact Hausdorff factors BPI suffices, even for product nonemptiness.

principles.name: Compact Hausdorff Tychonoff theorem
principles.definition: For every set I and every indexed family of compact Hausdorff topological spaces (X_i,τ_i), their Cartesian product with the product topology is compact (every open cover has a finite subcover).
principles.notes: This statement is equivalent to BPI and strictly weaker than AC over ZF. Empty factors/products are allowed; compactness alone does not imply nonemptiness. BPI also gives a nonempty product whenever all compact Hausdorff factors are nonempty. Thus adding a nonemptiness conclusion in this Hausdorff setting does not produce full AC. No compact Hausdorff topology can simply be assumed on an arbitrary set.

principles.name: No amorphous sets

principles.notes: No amorphous sets is weaker than the assertion that every infinite set is Dedekind-infinite: NDS ⇒ every Dedekind-finite set is finite ⇒ no amorphous sets. By contrast, if an amorphous set exists (the negation of this node), its cofinite filter is nonprincipal and is an ultrafilter, and that set is infinite Dedekind-finite. relations.proof_note: Under AC, well-order an infinite A and use cardinal arithmetic for infinite well-ordered cardinals. Conversely, for arbitrary A choose an infinite ordinal κ admitting no injection into A (for example, the larger of ω and the Hartogs ordinal h(A)).
